t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop web section as a flat straight-on UI mockup on deep navy. Left half: a macro 3D studio render, cropped off the left edge, of an exploded stack of frosted translucent membrane layers and a water sheet floating over a diagonal welded pipe, with a faint orbit ring and tiny monospace measurement annotations. Numbered steel-blue circular badges arc along its edge, each with a leader line fanning to a row of a four-column table on the right holding <CONTENT>, mono column headers, hairline rules, one row highlighted with a steel-blue band.
signature_idea: An exploded membrane-over-weld render fans six numbered leaders into a compliance table, one leader per industry row.
strengths: keeps the real four-column table, so comparison works
numbered leaders physically connect image to data
navy, mono headers and steel-blue badges fit the palette
exploded view speaks to engineering audiences
weaknesses: photo-real metal pipe reads as stainless steel, not polypropylene, wrong material story
gradient highlight bands and glow feel glossy and off-system
heavy caps industry names off Geist light
scattered tiny fake measurements are noise
leader mapping is arbitrary (layers do not correspond to industries)
brand_fit_why: Navy, mono headers, hairlines and steel-blue accent fit, but the glossy steel render, gradient bands and heavy caps drift from the flat, light, line-art brand and misrepresent PP.
